prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map lays out a tiled courtyard with an L-shaped ice-cream counter running from left-center to right at ~1.5–3 m, an interior recess behind the counter at ~3–4 m, and an open background corridor beyond 5 m on the right in frame 1 and left in frames 3–5. Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer walks toward the counter and turns left, bringing a person in a white shirt with a backpack from ~2 m on the left (frame 1) to within arm's reach at ~0.8 m directly in front (frame 2) before retreating to ~1.8–2.2 m (frames 3–5), while a seated person in the lower-left foreground enters at ~0.5–1.2 m (with another blurred head at <0.5 m occluding them in frame 4) and a standing person in an olive jacket remains ~1.5 m behind the seated person (~2.5–3 m from the camera). The person in the white shirt faces away toward the counter in frames 1–4 before turning in frame 5 to face and look toward the camera wearer with the counter within their left arm's reach, while the standing person on the left faces the camera and holds a cup within arm's reach, and a yellow ice-cream cone held by the camera wearer (or adjacent companion) appears at the bottom edge at ~0.4 m in frames 2–4. Compared to RGB alone, the depth gradient clearly separates the foreground silhouettes—especially the blurred close head in frame 4 and the bottom-edge cone—from the mid-ground seated person and counter planes without being distracted by the busy multicolored counter tiles. However, the map is unreliable on the glass display case on the right (flattening its transparent front and interior contents into a single plane) and merges the white-shirted person's backpack seamlessly into their torso silhouette.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates foreground and mid-ground people and small objects against a black background within the counter courtyard, tracking the primary person in a white shirt from the left at ~2 m (frame 1) to ~0.8 m in front (frame 2, where their lower legs are cropped out of view) and ~1.8–2.2 m in the center-right (frames 3–5) as they turn from facing the counter to facing the camera wearer. From frame 3 onward, as the camera turns left, it segments the cluster of people on the left separated by ~1–1.5 m from the white-shirted person and from each other: a seated person at ~1–1.2 m facing away-right, a standing person in an olive jacket behind them at ~2.5–3 m facing and looking toward the camera wearer while holding a cup within arm's reach, and a close foreground head at <0.5 m in the lower-left corner in frames 4–5 that partially occludes the seated person. In frames 4 and 5, it also detects the backpack on the white-shirted person's back, a worker behind the counter at ~3 m on the right (partially occluded by the display case and the white-shirted person's outstretched left arm), and small containers ('bottle') on the counter shelf at ~2.5–3 m. This map makes it easier than in RGB to distinguish the overlapping silhouettes in the left-hand group and to spot the partially occluded counter worker and shelf items in frames 4–5. However, the segmentation is unreliable in omitting the entire architectural counter structure, missing the backpack in frames 1–3 and 5 (merging it into the person mask), misclassifying a counter sign as a 'tv' in frame 2 and the seated person's head as a 'dog' in frame 4, and failing to detect the close foreground ice-cream cone at the bottom edge.
descriptions.pose: The pose map renders 2D body keypoints (yellow) and hand keypoints (magenta) primarily for the person in the white shirt across all 5 frames and adds a second skeleton for the standing person in the olive jacket on the left in frame 5 (~1.5 m to the left of and ~1 m farther than the white-shirted person). Across frames 1–4, the shoulder, hip, and head keypoints show the white-shirted person facing away toward the counter at ~2 m (frame 1), passing within arm's reach at ~0.8 m with their left arm reaching forward-left (frame 2, legs cropped below the knees), and standing at ~2 m with both arms at their sides (frames 3–4). In frame 5, the torso and facial keypoints rotate to face and look toward the camera wearer at ~1.5–1.8 m, with the left arm raised onto the counter within reach and the right arm hanging down to a dense cluster of magenta hand keypoints near the bottom edge, while the second skeleton on the left stands at ~2.5–3 m facing the camera with both elbows bent to hold an object near their face. Compared to RGB, the skeletal wireframe makes the exact body orientation, torso rotation between frames 4 and 5, and occluded limb positions through the loose shirt and backpack immediately explicit. However, the pose map is unreliable for full-scene coverage because it completely misses the seated person at ~1–1.2 m, the ultra-close foreground head at <0.5 m, the counter worker at ~3 m, and the standing person on the left in frames 2–4, while also omitting right-leg keypoints in frame 3 and nearly all hand keypoints except for a single right-hand cluster in frame 5.
